provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1862 points 'ut, et quae agenda sunt' where the 1962 points 'ut et, quae agenda sunt'; 1862 sets a semicolon after videant where the 1962 sets a comma; 1862 spells coelesti, the 1962 caelesti; the conclusions differ in length in the unusual direction: 1862 'Per Dominum nostrum.', 1962 'Per Dominum.'. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 13809-13815, which prints 'Vota, quaesumus Domine, supplicantis populi coelesti pietate prosequere: vt, & quae agenda sunt, videant: & ad implenda quae viderint, conualescant' - agreeing with the 1862's comma placement against the 1962's.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Vota, quaesumus, Domine, supplicantis populi caelesti pietate prosequere: ut
et, quae agenda sunt, videant, et ad implenda, quae viderint, convalescant.
Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
